meta.research_basis: PitchBook, launch coverage via PitchBook news, web search; noetive.ai could not be opened
meta.alert: Five weeks out of stealth and built inside lead investor Eclipse, which recruited the founders; CEO Amir Frenkel is also Eclipse's Chief AI Officer [2,4]. noetive.ai could not be opened here, so product detail rests on launch coverage and PitchBook.

company.name: Noetive
company.one_liner: AI agents plus in-house floor sensors that take over operational decisions such as production planning, positioned as a decision layer above a plant's ERP and MES.

sections.company_product: Agents run on top of a customer's existing systems and make operational decisions end to end, fed by a multimodal sensing pod Noetive designs [2] {CR}. The company says design partners in manufacturing, logistics, energy and data centers use it [2] {CR}.

technology.text: A core model (the "brain") learns how an operation runs from system data and pod signals, acts, and learns from outcomes; each deployment is meant to improve the shared model [2,3] {CR}.
bullets: **Not disclosed:** in-house model or agents on frontier models; what the pod senses; write-back to ERP or advice only {UNK}.

**Likely moat, if any:** plan-versus-actual data compounding across sites, not the model {INF}. The pod adds data rivals lack, but also hardware cost and, in German plants, works-council approval for monitoring devices {INF}.

market.text: Wedge appears to be production planning in process plants, today run in ERP or APS tools, spreadsheets and planner judgment {INF}.
bullets: **Palantir AIP / Warp Speed:** scheduling and production workflows over ERP, MES and PLM data, sold to manufacturers [6].
**Archetype AI:** sensor-data foundation model (Newton); $35M round Nov 2025 [5]. Closest on physical sensing.
**SAP, Kinaxis, o9:** the planning suites Noetive sits on, likely to add agents themselves {INF}.

sections.team_financing: CEO Amir Frenkel spent nearly a decade as a Meta VP over AI applied research, after Google (Glass), Amazon, TI and Palm [4]. CPO Dan Barak founded Stackbit, sold to Netlify, after product roles at Lyft and Meta [3]. Eclipse led the $41M seed [1], joined by 19 others including Craft, Westly, Gigascale and angels Bosworth and Schroepfer [1]. No founder with plant operations background disclosed {UNK}.
sections.traction: One named partner: Steuben Foods, an aseptic food and beverage manufacturer, whose CEO Menachem Katz says planning that ran monthly over a week now runs daily in minutes [2]. A design-partner quote, not a measured result; paid status and vendor effort undisclosed {UNK}. PitchBook tags it as generating revenue, no figures [1].

perspective.interesting: Frontier-AI team aimed at operational decisions, with a customer CEO describing a step change within months. The bet: sensing plus outcome data compounds into a model incumbents cannot copy {INF}.
perspective.validate: Product versus forward-deployed engineering per site; and Eclipse dependence (it built the company, led the round and employs the CEO): board, terms, room for an outside lead.
perspective.fit: Fits the industrial AI thesis; no portfolio overlap found. Planning and inbound logistics at Volkswagen Group component or PowerCo plants are a plausible later test {INF}.

questions.question: At Steuben, what does the system decide versus recommend, which systems does it write back to, and how many Noetive engineer-days a week does it still take?
questions.why: Separates a product from forward-deployed services.

questions.question: What does the pod capture that ERP and MES data missed, and how much of the Steuben gain remains without it?
questions.why: Tests whether the hardware is the moat or a deployment drag.

questions.question: What did the brain learn at one design partner that made the next deployment faster, and how do you measure that?
questions.why: Tests the cross-customer learning claim the thesis rests on.
